rubric.why: Identifies a taxon as a unit or rank in biological classification.
rubric.description: A taxon is a unit or rank of classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a classification unit or rank.

rubric.why: States that a taxon is a group of organisms.
rubric.description: It is a group of organisms at any level of classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it consists of organisms.

modelAnswer: A taxon is a unit of biological classification.
It is a group of organisms at any level of classification.

items.followUp: What are the main stages of the cell cycle?

rubric.why: Recognises the reproductive role of germ-line cells.
rubric.description: Germ-line cells give rise to gametes or sex cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking germ-line cells with gametes or sex cells.

rubric.why: Identifies the cells as reproductive cells or their precursors.
rubric.description: They are reproductive cells, or cells that produce reproductive cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying their reproductive nature.

modelAnswer: Germ-line cells are reproductive cells that give rise to gametes.
They pass genetic information to the next generation.

items.followUp: State one difference between mitosis and meiosis in the number of daughter cells produced.

rubric.why: Describes mitosis as one division producing two genetically identical cells.
rubric.description: Mitosis is one cell division that produces two genetically identical daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the division and outcome.

rubric.why: Describes meiosis as two divisions producing four haploid cells.
rubric.description: Meiosis consists of two divisions and produces four haploid daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the divisions and outcome.

modelAnswer: Mitosis is one cell division in which one parent cell forms two genetically identical daughter cells.
Meiosis consists of two successive divisions and forms four haploid daughter cells.

items.followUp: What role do spindle fibres play during cell division?

rubric.why: Identifies the centrosome's role in organising structures involved in cell division.
rubric.description: Centrosomes organise spindle fibres (and asters) during cell division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming spindle fibres or asters.

rubric.why: States the result of spindle organisation during division.
rubric.description: The spindle helps separate chromosomes or chromatids towards opposite poles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing chromosome or chromatid separation.

modelAnswer: Centrosomes organise the spindle fibres during cell division.
The spindle fibres help separate chromosomes towards opposite poles of the cell.

items.followUp: What is meant by the energy currency of the cell?

rubric.why: Identifies ATP as the cell's energy currency.
rubric.description: ATP is known as the energy currency of the cell.

rubric.why: Explains ATP's role in making energy available for cellular activities.
rubric.description: ATP stores and transfers energy for cellular activities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ATP stores, transfers, or supplies energy.

modelAnswer: ATP is the energy currency of the cell.
It stores and transfers energy for cellular activities.

items.followUp: Give one example each of an anabolic and a catabolic process.

rubric.why: States that anabolism builds complex substances from simpler ones.
rubric.description: Anabolism is the building of complex substances from simpler substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the direction of synthesis.

rubric.why: States that catabolism breaks down complex substances and releases energy.
rubric.description: Catabolism breaks complex substances into simpler ones, releasing energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for breakdown and energy release.

modelAnswer: Anabolism is the building of complex substances from simpler substances and requires energy.
Catabolism is the breakdown of complex substances into simpler ones and releases energy.

items.followUp: What is an enzyme, and how does it affect a chemical reaction?

rubric.why: States that biocatalysts increase the rate of biochemical reactions.
rubric.description: Biocatalysts speed up biochemical reactions by lowering activation energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for faster reactions or lower activation energy.

rubric.why: Gives a further benefit of biocatalysts, such as specificity, working under mild conditions, or being reusable.
rubric.description: They are specific and can work under mild conditions without being used up.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid additional benefit.

modelAnswer: Biocatalysts, such as enzymes, speed up biochemical reactions by lowering their activation energy.
They are specific and can work under mild conditions without being used up.

items.followUp: Name the enzyme in saliva and state what it digests.

rubric.why: Identifies chewing as a function of the oral cavity.
rubric.description: The teeth in the oral cavity chew food and break it into smaller pieces.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for chewing or mechanical breakdown.

rubric.why: Identifies the start of starch digestion in the oral cavity.
rubric.description: Saliva mixes with food, and salivary amylase begins starch digestion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking saliva or amylase with starch digestion.

modelAnswer: The oral cavity receives food and breaks it into smaller pieces by chewing.
Saliva mixes with the food, and salivary amylase begins the digestion of starch.
